title: Phone clock check against server time (prevent device date problems)
description: Owner 2026-10-23. App measures clock offset from the HTTP Date header of server responses on each sync (no new endpoint; or include server_time in /api/v1/app/android/latest), stores the last offset. If |offset| > 5 min: persistent notice 'Your phone's date/time is wrong (X ahead/behind). Set Date & time to automatic' with a button opening Android Date & time settings (Linking/IntentLauncher ACTION_DATE_SETTINGS); stronger when > 1 day. Form date validation ('not in the future', 1 July cap, today in age calculations) and the device envelope startedAt/completedAt use offset-corrected time where an offset is known; offline uses the last offset; never-synced: no warning. Server: accept and store the measured offset with each upload (device envelope field, additive) so coders/supervisors can see skewed submissions; flag uploads whose completedAt is in the server's future beyond tolerance. Policy note in docs/policy/field-data-collection.md or offline-api-contract.md first. Tests both sides.
notes: Owner rule: if the measured offset is MORE THAN 4 HOURS, block data entry: no new registration, no new interview, no editing an existing draft/revision, until the clock is fixed and a fresh check passes (Re-check button after the user opens Date & time settings). Still allowed: viewing, Send now/Refresh (sync is how the offset is measured), Settings, Export errors, sign-out guard. If the block is detected while a form is open: save what is typed immediately (never lose data), then show the blocking screen. 5 min..4 h: warning only (as above). Offline with a stored offset > 4 h: stay blocked until a check passes. Never measured (never synced): no block. Policy text must state the 4 h rule.
close_reason: Closed

Same component on web InterviewScreen (shared engine). Depends on digitva-3nui (refusal storage). Bundle with digitva-e49e (same screens). Tests: list built from engine issues and server fields, Go navigates and scrolls to top of the question, hidden-question case.

title: Native offline attachments (audio, images, documents): encrypted store, resumable upload, re-encode and security checks
description: Owner decisions 2026-10-20: (1) scope: audio narration plus images and documents (confirm which instrument questions need image/file; Id10476_audio is the only one confirmed). (2) A case with a missing file cannot be submitted: block final submit until every attachment is uploaded; the case stays on the phone and in the outstanding-work report. (3) Resumable/chunked upload on the server (50 MB single PUT is not acceptable on rural networks). (4) No antivirus first; instead server-side re-encode of media (audio/image transcode to canonical formats, strip metadata) and security checks incl. decompression/deflate-bomb protection, magic-byte type checks, size/duration/pixel caps. Audit (2026-10-20): server web path PUT /api/v1/intake/drafts/<id>/attachments/<client_attachment_id> exists (web_intake_attachment_service.py); device path has no pre-submit upload (device interview becomes a server draft only at POST /intake/submissions); native has no capture (src/platform.ts), no encrypted file store (interviewerDb.ts is SQLCipher answers only), no upload queue (sync.ts), RECORD_AUDIO blocked in app.json. Plan: policy baseline in docs/policy first; then server device-attachment path + resumable upload + re-encode/validation; encrypted chunked file store; local attachments table; audio capture; image/file capture; upload queue before submit; quota + outstanding report. Start only after the current UI batch is committed (migrations chain on committed revisions).
notes:
Owner 2026-10-22: phone (digitva-collect) first: audio narration Id10476_audio + narrative photo; web keeps its placeholder for now. Queue after the current collect work (consent 0vgh, collection-only build cpx5).

Native audio recording (and photo/document capture) needed: record/playback/re-record, size/duration limits per odk-attachment-intake-limits policy, stored encrypted locally, uploaded with the interview through the existing attachment path, works offline. Also: when an _audio question and its text twin share the same prompt (Id10476_audio / Id10476), show the prompt once with both answer modes; long interviewer instruction notes collapse to one line after first view.

title: Reopening a web draft shows empty answers and autosave can overwrite the saved ones
description: Confirmed 2026-09-29 on dev: draft eca5d80d has 48 saved answers on the server (GET /intake/api/drafts/<id>) but the form shows them empty. The package calls draftStore.load() only when its navigation adapter restores a position (create-who-va-form.tsx restoredNavigation effect); DigitVA's page sets draft-id + draftStore and never gets load(). va_intake_form.html fills lastSaved only inside load(), so the first autosave treats every section as changed and PATCHes the form's empty state -> saved answers overwritten. Predates the redesign (same logic at 2c98f2a). Fix in the host: load the envelope before mounting and hand it to the element (setData / initial data API), seed lastSaved, and never PATCH a section the form has not loaded; add a regression test (route/JS) and a browser check; check server PATCH semantics for empty sections.
close_reason: Form loads the draft on mount and blocks every save until restore settles (and for the whole mount if load fails); same-instrument language switch keeps answers; host refuses to PATCH before its baseline loads. Verified on dev: new draft survives reload and a language switch; eca5d80d's 48 answers display and are unchanged on the server.

title: Suggest the age group from the dates and confirm a mismatch
description: Owner 2026-10-23: the 'What age group corresponds to the deceased?' question (age_group: neonate/child/adult) can be derived from date of birth and date of death. If the interviewer picks a group that contradicts the derived one, show a confirmation ('The dates suggest Child (about 4 years). Keep Adult?' Keep / Use suggestion); re-check when a date changes later. Never override a confirmed choice; record nothing extra in the payload. Tests: exact, years-only, ambiguous, mismatch confirm, date edit after choice.

title: Web interview autosave loops on csrf_failed after the cookie session dies, with no visible sign-in prompt
description: Staging 2026-10-23 08:30-09:05 UTC: one Windows Chrome user's PATCH /api/v1/intake/drafts/affd98f4-... got 400 (68 B) about once a minute. 68 B is exactly the csrf_failed body with 'The CSRF session token is missing.' (app/routes/va_errors.py:10, flask-wtf; the app-level CSRF hook app/__init__.py:285 runs before auth, so a dead session gives 400 not 401). Client: vendor/who-va-2022 create-who-va-form.tsx:935 autosaves every 20s (Chrome throttles a hidden tab to ~1/min); ServerDraftStore.flush (mobile/digitva-collect/src/client/serverDraftStore.ts:171) keeps the draft pending and calls onError on every failure, so it retries forever; requestJson (src/api.ts:683) refreshes the token via /me/access once, which cannot revive a dead session. Only a text banner is set (InterviewScreen.tsx:455); no redirect/re-login, no local copy. Answers since the last good save survive only in the open tab's memory: closing it loses them. Proposed fix: (1) on csrf_failed/401 from a draft save, stop the timer and show a blocking 'sign in again' dialog (re-auth in a popup/new tab, then flush) ; (2) mirror pending answers to sessionStorage/IndexedDB so a reload recovers them; (3) exponential backoff. Also find why the session ended (30 min PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME, config.py:145; Redis/sessions table purge?). Related: digitva-oxvt.
notes:
Staging logs 2026-10-23 (minerva_app, IP 110.235.232.172): NOT once a minute - 298 failed PATCHes in the 08:00 hour (~1 per 2s from 08:20:28), 9 more to 09:05:28; POST /drafts/<id>/submit also 400/68B at 08:23:42, 08:23:48, 08:25:51, 08:26:36, 08:29:16, 09:05:25 (user tried to submit 6x, none went through). Container started 08:18:05, restarted 08:27:22 (logs before 08:18 gone). No valogin from this IP; after a plain page load GET /intake/ at 09:05:33 and /intake/form/<id> at 09:05:45 the PATCH returned 200 at once. So the cookie session was alive; the page lacked a usable CSRF token (68B = 'The CSRF session token is missing.'), and a reload fixed it. No /me/access calls from this IP during 08:20-08:37, i.e. the client's one-shot csrf refresh (src/api.ts:683) did not run or the deployed bundle predates it. Open: why the session lost its csrf_token around the 08:18 restart; answers typed after the last good save were in tab memory only and the 09:05 reload may have discarded them.
Staging bundle check: current entry-*.js (built 2026-10-23 08:04 UTC; image 08:15:47; container up 08:17:45) HAS the csrf refresh retry. The previous image was built 2026-10-19 10:40 UTC, before the retry commit cac5d57a7 (2026-10-22). The user's tab was opened under the old bundle and kept running it across the 08:18 deploy: it had no retry, hence no /me/access and an endless loop until the 09:05 reload. Fixes to add: version check so a tab running an old bundle after a deploy shows 'reload' (keeping answers), plus the loop/backoff/local-copy items. Still open: why the old tab's session had no csrf_token after the deploy.
Session-loss cause (strong hypothesis): staging restore. scripts/loadtest/restore.sh pg_restore --clean replaces the whole DB, including the server-side session table va_sessions (SESSION_TYPE=sqlalchemy, config.py:162), with the pre-test backup, then restarts app (container up 08:17:45, gunicorn 08:18:05; first 400 08:20:28). A restored va_sessions row can be a snapshot of this user's session from before the page minted its CSRF token: logged in, but no csrf_token in the session = flask-wtf 'The CSRF session token is missing.' (68 B). A page reload mints a new token into that same session, which is why 09:05 recovered with no login. Fits every log line. Not verified against the DB. Mitigations: (a) restore.sh: truncate va_sessions after restore so users sign in cleanly (owner's go; staging script); (b) client items above. Production restores would do the same to open sessions.
close_reason: App CSRF hook answers 401 not_authenticated on /api/v1 (cookie, no session) before CSRF; authenticated stays 400 csrf_failed. Server side only; client pending. Test in tests/routes/test_api_v1_credentials.py

title: Give the SmartVA Celery worker container a lower CPU weight (cpu_shares), since nice inside the container has no effect
description:
Staging A/B 2026-10-23 on d120dae27 (t4g.medium, 2 vCPU), identical 4-minute 200-user runs, p50/p95 ms.
- Worker paused: available 142/630, allocate 129/653, doris.process 101/551; 27.1 req/s.
- Worker running at NI=10 (digitva-295w, landed): available 569-592/~1800-1970, allocate 550-607/~1760-2010, doris.process 583-631/~1670-1890; 24.7-24.9 req/s. Same as without nice (551/1843, 529/1644, 547/1886).
Cause: each container is its own cgroup, and both minerva_app and minerva_celery_worker had cpu.weight=100, so niceness only ranks processes inside the worker's own cgroup. A DB wait sampler during the run (165 samples) showed 92% of busy backends 'idle in transaction / ClientRead' and no lock blocking: requests are slow in Python, not in Postgres.
Live test: docker update --cpu-shares 128 on the staging worker (cgroup cpu.weight 21 vs the app's 100) gave available 252/1092, allocate 227/1081, doris.process 195/945, intake 542/1423; 26.5 req/s, 0 5xx; SmartVA queue stayed at 0-11.
Change: add cpu_shares: 128 (or lower; test it) to minerva_celery_worker in docker-compose.yml and demo_celery_worker in docker-compose.demo.yml. Keep nice (harmless). Extend tests/test_celery_worker_recycle.py to assert it.
Verify after deploy: /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/docker-<id>.scope/cpu.weight is about 21 for the worker and 100 for the app.
Note: docker update --cpu-shares 0 does NOT reset the value; recreate the container instead.
close_reason: Landed: cpu_shares 128 on both Celery workers (nice kept); staging A/B showed request p50 roughly halved while the worker runs

title: Run the SmartVA Celery worker at lower CPU priority so requests keep their latency
description: Staging load test 2026-10-23 (t4g.medium, 2 vCPU, main f05091920). Identical 4-minute 200-user runs: worker PAUSED gave p50/p95 intake 388/913 ms, available 142/630, allocate 129/653, finalize 197/741, doris.process 101/551 at 27.1 req/s. Worker RUNNING gave intake 909/2102, available 551/1843, allocate 529/1644, finalize 743/1967, doris.process 547/1886 at 25.6 req/s; 0 5xx in both. Cause: the box is CPU-saturated (gunicorn alone 155-180% of 2 cores), and the now-fast warm and batched SmartVA worker (25-50% CPU) processes every interview immediately; on 2026-10-22 it fell ~3,300 tasks behind instead. Smallest fix: start the worker with lower scheduling priority (e.g. 'nice -n 10 celery ... worker' in docker-compose.yml, or os.nice in a worker_process_init signal), so gunicorn wins CPU and SmartVA catches up in idle gaps. Verify with the same A/B harness (scratchpad lt_run.py, --duration 240 --ramp 60 --think 10): target latency near the paused run, with the SmartVA queue draining within minutes after load. Alternative: a 4 vCPU instance.
close_reason: Landed: workers under nice -n 10 (staging A/B pending); allocation locks workflow row before insert on every path, deadlock -> 409; c5e7a9b1d3f6 drops an INVALID leftover index before building

CORRECTED 2026-10-21: the device-local Axum server (digitva-server) IS accepted as the app's own backend (owner: 'the local app will need a local server'), within the limits of docs/policy/offline-bundle-and-transfer.md section 10 'Local server requirements' (loopback only, per-launch bearer on every route, Host/Origin checks, no CORS, no-store, never mint server ids). Data is pushed by (1) HTTPS to existing intake endpoints with a device bearer token, or (2) an offline bundle file. All server-side work is ours; the offline team builds a client crate (bundle writer) on a spec we propose. Authoritative contract: docs/policy/offline-api-contract.md (Offline API contract v1). Policy: docs/policy/offline-bundle-and-transfer.md. Related: digitva-athy (consent), digitva-kzyp (identifiers), digitva-ke83 (offline desktop epic), digitva-jkvl (offline attachments), PII baseline docs/policy/pii-encryption-at-rest.md, sealed format docs/policy/pii-envelope-format.md.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-10-21 (Q5 of 5): bundle spec defaults Q1-Q9 accepted as written (see 'Owner decisions (resolved 2026-10-21)' at the end of docs/policy/offline-bundle-and-transfer.md). Q6 clarified: offline app keeps its own LOCAL case list (cases it registered/interviewed/codes); NO server-provided case list in station config; server-to-station case download out of scope. Q10: consent at registration for web/Expo (digitva-athy).
DECIDED 2026-10-21 (reviewer Q1): never-online / paste-enrolled station trust comes from the ONBOARDING process, where a responsible person from that station is identified. Accept the admin-signed roster in the station config as the attestation (no per-user online sign-in required), and record the identified station custodian (name, role, contact, onboarding date, who verified) in enrolment and in the signed station config; add the weaker-trust note to the threat table. Remaining reviewer questions pending: sandbox data never ingestable; local MCCD PDF provisional; station registration informant fields none before interview consent; HTTPS purge channel; local supervisor corrections disabled when provisioned.
DECIDED 2026-10-21 (reviewer Q2-Q6): Q2 ingestion only from an ONBOARDED station; sandbox/pre-onboarding data is not guessed into a project (never remapped). Q3 offline-coded MCCD PDF is NOT marked provisional or disabled: coded is coded; any review goes through the existing review process with its logging. Q4 consent is ALSO taken at registration on the station (same as web/Expo); the interview reuses it (re-ask only if the informant is a different person); consent record keyed by case, client_draft_id optional. Q5 HTTPS purge channel = signed station config served to the device token (purge list of consent ids), same format as the bundle path. Q6 on a provisioned station the user MAY do supervisor-style corrections locally (edit death details, edit identifiers after interview); the server ACCEPTS those edits with the user id in the audit log: needs new record types death_correction and identifiers_set (bundle) + HTTPS equivalent; authorization basis = admin-signed station roster with a station role (e.g. station_supervisor) on an enrolled station with a known custodian; all server validation (identifier rules, duplicates warn, closed-case, stale) still applies; audit records user id, station id, device id, bundle id, authorized_by=station_roster. Consent WITHDRAWAL stays web-only (not changed by Q6). Threat table must note the widened correction authority.
2026-10-21: Offline API contract v1 written (docs/policy/offline-api-contract.md, proposed): endpoint tables with status markers, consent object and consent-config (refusal_behaviour, retention, witness_allowed defined), identifiers list shapes and generic identifier_in_use warnings (no other case ids), purge via station config/receipts and GET /api/v1/intake/station-config on the device bearer, local server requirements, standalone = sandbox, sealed_field_ids served in station config. Bundle spec amended: death_registration.consent_client_id and informant-field rule, no bundle record for later identifier sets/register corrections (HTTPS only), paste-enrolled actor refinement of Q4, section 10 Local server requirements. OWNER DECISIONS PENDING (contract section 12): 1 paste-enrolled actor trust = signed roster; 2 sandbox data never ingestable; 3 local MCCD PDF 'provisional'; 4 no station-registration informant fields before interview consent; 5 HTTPS purge = station config over device bearer; 6 local supervisor corrections disabled when provisioned. Message to offline session: docs/kb/offline-session-message-2026-10-21.md. Epic title still says 'no server-side code' (not changed).
2026-10-21: owner decisions 1-7 APPLIED to docs (contract section 12 now 'Owner decisions (resolved 2026-10-21)'; no pending markers left): onboarding + custodian {name, designation, phone, email, onboarded_on, verified_by_user_id} in enrolment and signed station config; ingest only from an onboarded station (whole-bundle refusal station_not_onboarded); no 'provisional' MCCD PDF; station consent at registration (consent keyed by case, client_draft_id null for registration consent, interview reuses, re-ask for a different informant); HTTPS purge via GET /intake/station-config, same list format as receipts; new bundle records death_correction and identifiers_set (contract 4.2) + station roster path on PATCH /intake/deaths/<id> and PUT /intake/cases/<id>/identifiers (acting_role station_supervisor, reason, client_id; if_updated_at or base_client_id for stale; closed cases refused; death_correction refused case_completed after an interview completes, as for every caller); audit authorized_by=station_roster with device_id (= station id), station_config_id, bundle_id; roster in contract 4.1 (gb8w.8). Withdrawal stays web only. Offline message rewritten with DROP/ADD lists. Docs uncommitted; commit <hash to follow>.

title: DPDP Act 2023 consent from the respondent (informant): notice, consent record, refusal, withdrawal, offline capture
description: Owner 2026-10-21: DPDP consent from respondent needed. Capture before informant personal data is saved (proposed at death registration; owner to confirm), notice versioned and in the respondent language, append-only consent record (granted/refused, time, notice version+language, recorded by, mode), refusal keeps interview without informant contact details, withdrawal by supervisor/DM with erasure+audit, offline queue carries consent. Needs policy baseline in docs/policy first; legal review of DPDP scope (deceased data, research exemptions) not done. Related: digitva-kzyp, PII encryption work.
notes:
Owner 2026-10-21: consent variables are defined at PROJECT level: consent required (y/n), versioned notice text per language (old versions kept; each consent record points to the exact version), itemised purposes (required/optional each), data fields covered and refusal behaviour, retention and expiry action (erase/lock), withdrawal contact and who may record withdrawal, allowed consent modes (spoken/tap/signed, witness), DPO details. Configured in Project Setup beside identifier types; every change audited. Roles: admin, project_pi, data_manager of the project.
Owner 2026-10-21: notice must show contacts: a deletion/exclusion email (+phone), a DISTRICT-level contact (per district org unit, falls back to central team), the mentoring institution contact, and the central team contact. Project-level settings hold deletion email, mentor institution, central team, DPO; district contact is stored per district unit. Changes audited and create a new notice version. Requests received by email are logged on the case (who/when/what) and actioned by supervisor or data manager. Draft text: docs/policy/respondent-consent-notice-draft.md.
Owner 2026-10-21: OFFLINE APP consent is taken AT THE INTERVIEW by the interviewer in the app (offline app is simple: interviewer interviews and takes consent, coder codes, data is pushed). Open: web/Expo death reporters can save informant phone/address at REGISTRATION before the interview; decide whether consent is also taken at registration or those fields are treated as the reporter's report record (legal/workflow call). No device-side withdrawal: withdrawal recorded on web, server tells device to purge.
2026-10-21: offline bundle and transfer spec proposed in docs/policy/offline-bundle-and-transfer.md: consent record type in bundles and optional consent object on POST /intake/submissions (422 consent_required only when the project requires consent and covered informant data is present), GET /api/v1/intake/consent-config, consent tables sketched (mas_consent_notice_versions, va_consent_records append-only, va_consent_record_purposes), notice_sha256 on every record, signed station config carries notice versions and district contacts. DECIDED 2026-10-21 (Q1 of 5): for web/Expo death registration, consent is taken AT REGISTRATION whenever informant name/phone/address are entered (same notice, same append-only record keyed by case). The interview reuses it and re-asks only if the informant is a different person. Informant fields cannot be saved at registration without a granted record (422 consent_required). Offline app: consent at the interview (see digitva-gb8w and docs/policy/offline-bundle-and-transfer.md).
2026-10-21: consent is taken at registration on the offline station too (same as web/Expo); interview reuses it. Withdrawal stays web-only; station purges via the signed station config purge list (served to the device token on HTTPS).
2026-10-21: consent contract fixed in docs/policy/offline-api-contract.md section 5: one consent object (client_id, client_draft_id, notice_version_id, notice_language, notice_sha256 of the served text string, decision, purposes all sorted, mode, witness_present, supersedes_client_id, recorded_at) on POST /intake/submissions, POST /intake/deaths (registration consent, client_draft_id null) and bundle consent records; 422 consent_required / consent_invalid with fields ['consent'], 409 conflict on client_id reuse with other content; no consent_status on case replies. consent-config shapes: witness_allowed bool, retention {period_days, expiry_action erase|lock}, refusal_behaviour 'interview_without_informant_data'. Withdrawal web only; station purge via station config/receipt purge lists (HTTPS: station config on the device bearer, pending owner confirmation). Server work: this bead (registration consent, withdrawal, purge emission) and digitva-gb8w.3.
Owner 2026-10-22 (web): consent screen is required when the project turns it on (Project Setup 'Require respondent consent'); off = no screen. Shown before a direct web interview and at death registration before informant details. Notice seeded from docs/policy/respondent-consent-notice-draft.md (en + hi), editable per project in Project Setup, marked 'pending legal review' until the owner approves. Refusal: interview proceeds without informant contact details. Withdrawal later. Queued after digitva-oxvt (InterviewScreen).

title: Death registration identifiers: per-project types (civil registration, MCCD, certificate) with regex validation, supervisor add/edit later, shown in lists
description: Owner 2026-10-20: a reported death can carry several registration identifiers (Civil Registration Number, MCCD Number, Certificate Number, etc.). Identifier TYPES and their validation REGEX are configured per project; the rules apply when a death is reported. Identifiers may be absent at report time and are added/edited LATER (numbers are often generated days later) by a supervisor for any death in their scope (and by the reporter for own deaths if policy allows: open question). Death lists show the identifiers. Entry field is monospaced. Schema: new master (mas_*) for identifier types per project incl. regex + label + required flag, and a per-death values table (additive migration, audited, unique per death+type, history kept). Policy baseline docs/policy first. Build after the current UI batch is committed (migration chain).
notes:
Owner 2026-10-20 (addendum): per-type validation can include min/max length and character type (numeric / alphanumeric / etc.) in addition to an optional regex. Values are ALWAYS captured and stored in CAPITALS (normalise on client as typed and again on the server; uniqueness compares the normalised value).
Owner 2026-10-20 (answers, one by one): Q-CSV: registration numbers ARE included in the data-manager CSV export, only for exporters with PII access in that project, and the export is audited (exception to the direct-identifier-free bulk extract rule; record in docs/policy/death-registration-identifiers.md and case-list-views.md). Remaining open: duplicate number warn vs block; who may edit after interview complete; project_pi may configure types; collaborator_pii sees values; writes on cancelled/duplicate cases; google-re2 second guard.
Owner 2026-10-20: a number already on another death in the same project WARNS (user may continue). Message shows the other case id and unit AND the reporting user's name and designation (cadre) of that case ('This number is already on case X (unit Y), reported by <name> - <designation>'); only to roles allowed to see reporter identity (supervisor scope; check should_redact_pii); also raises a possible-duplicate hint for the supervisor.
Owner 2026-10-20: who may add/edit registration numbers AFTER the interview is complete: In-charge (site_pi at a unit; also covers supervisors in scope), the death reporter on their own deaths, the interviewer on cases they interviewed, and data managers within their project scope. All writes audited (map_case_transitions identifiers_set). Not decided: project_pi (as configurer), collaborator_pii visibility, writes on cancelled/duplicate cases.
Owner 2026-10-20: identifier types (names, length/char rules, regex, required-at-report) may be configured by admin, project_pi and data_manager (within their project); all changes audited; regex still validated at save time (safe subset, ReDoS guard). Still open: collaborator_pii visibility of values; writes on cancelled/confirmed-duplicate cases; google-re2 second guard.
Owner 2026-10-20: values visible to roles with PII access in the project, and to collaborator_pii; everyone else (coders, reviewers, roles without PII) sees only a has-number / missing badge, never the value. Still open: writes on cancelled/confirmed-duplicate cases; google-re2 second guard.
Owner 2026-10-20: registration numbers need COLUMN-LEVEL ENCRYPTION in the DB. Design direction (follow app/services/totp_service.py): AES-256-GCM, key via HKDF from a dedicated env key (new PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY, never AUTH_FACTOR key reuse), versioned ciphertext prefix + key id for rotation, AAD bound to death_id+type so a value cannot be moved between rows; plaintext only in memory after authz; blind index = HMAC-SHA256 (separate key) over the NORMALISED (upper-cased, trimmed) value for duplicate warn, 'has number' and exact search; no plaintext in logs, audit changes (store only hash/last4 mask), error messages or exports other than the audited CSV for PII exporters; regex/length/char validation runs on plaintext BEFORE encrypt. Q7 (writes on cancelled/duplicate) left at default read-only.
Owner 2026-10-20 (Q7 answered, supersedes the earlier default): registration numbers MAY still be added/edited on cancelled or confirmed-duplicate deaths, by supervisors and in-charge only (audited). Reporter/interviewer/data manager stay read-only on closed cases. All identifier questions are now answered except google-re2 as a second regex guard.
Owner 2026-10-20: use post-quantum cryptography for the identifier columns. Design: AES-256-GCM data cipher (already quantum-resistant), DEKs wrapped with hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 (FIPS 203), KEM private key in a separate secret store, algorithm-id/key-id prefix for crypto-agility and rotation by re-wrapping, HMAC-SHA-512 blind index with its own key, ML-DSA (FIPS 204) only if signatures are needed. Library choice (liboqs-python vs cryptography with ML-KEM) is an OPEN owner decision; adding it needs approval + rebuild of app/celery worker/celery beat images.
2026-10-20 library check: installed cryptography 46.0.5 (OpenSSL 3.5.5) has no mlkem/mldsa modules; pyca/cryptography 48.0.0 (2026-05-04) added ML-KEM and ML-DSA on OpenSSL>=3.5 wheels; PyPI latest 50.0.2. Decision: raise pin to cryptography>=48 (target 50.0.2) at build time; liboqs not needed; requires uv add + rebuild app/celery worker/celery beat images + review of 46->50 breaking changes (ODK Fernet and TOTP AES-GCM use cryptography).
Owner 2026-10-21 decisions: Q2 Aadhaar reduction rolled out by ONE controlled sweep with backup gate (not gradual). See the new rollout bead.
2026-10-21: station roster users may correct identifiers after the interview on provisioned stations; server accepts with user id in audit (see digitva-gb8w). Authorization basis there is the signed station roster, not a supervising grant.
2026-10-21: date of death (Id10023) stays readable for staff; sealed set gets a never-sealed list; research export keeps month+year only. See the research export bead.

Today: draft editable by its author until submit; a submitted web/device interview cannot be edited at all (web-intake.md 'Editing a submitted web case is not supported'); supervisor reopen is a case-state move only; ODK forms change through ODK Central edits picked up by sync, with protected states once coding starts and a needs-revision writeback. Owner 2026-10-04 Q1: after upload and before coding starts, only the interviewer who did it may open a revision; a reason is required; no approval step, no supervisor gate. Versions kept, never overwritten; each records who, when, why, which answers changed.
Owner 2026-10-04 Q2: once coding starts the interview is locked for the interviewer; only a coder or reviewer can send it back for revision (same behaviour as ODK needs-revision), which reopens it for the interviewer; coding restarts on the new version.
Owner 2026-10-04 Q3: after final COD the interview is locked; only a supervisor or admin may reopen it, with a reason; the interviewer then revises, the case is recoded from scratch, the earlier COD kept in history (as ODK admin reset/reopen).
Owner 2026-10-04 Q4: the interviewer can revise on the phone and in the browser. The app downloads the submitted answers on demand when the interviewer taps Revise; the revision uploads as a new version, offline-safe and idempotent like any interview. Defaults (not asked): no time window, revisable until coding starts; superseded copies are not revisable; locked prefill answers stay locked; each version carries its own answer hash.
Owner 2026-10-04 Q5: match ODK exactly. The interviewer may revise through the active coding states (coding_in_progress, partial_coding_saved, coder_step1_saved); a revision there drops unfinished coding and re-routes to smartva_pending. Lock starts at coder_finalized (ODK-protected states). Policy: docs/policy/interview-revisions.md.
Owner 2026-10-04 Q6: a partially_completed submission (case paused) is finished by revising the same submission, not a fresh draft. A revision that changes the outcome to completed runs submit_draft's completion branch (case -> submitted, death.va_sid set, enters coding); the partial version stays in history.
Owner 2026-10-04 Q7: an interviewer revision that releases a coder's allocation gets its own audit/KPI reason (interviewer_revision), separate from ODK's va_allocation_released_during_datasync.
Owner 2026-10-04: after a coder/reviewer send-back or supervisor reopen, the interviewer's revision restarts coding at once (no DM accept step): the DM accept-upstream block is extracted and run by the revision with a system actor. title: Per-project OAuth2/OIDC SSO with claim-to-role mapping
description:
Each project can federate sign-in to its own identity provider (Keycloak, Auth0, Okta, Entra or any standards-compliant OIDC/OAuth2 AS) while the DigitVA password form keeps working. Administrators configure, per project, which token claim or audience maps to which DigitVA role and to which project site or organization unit; roles and scope resolve into va_user_access_grants and are reconciled on every SSO login. Project sites and org units carry a per-connection external SSO id so claim values resolve to local scope.

Decisions with the owner (2026-09-26): user linking configurable per connection (existing_only default, or link_or_create_by_email); SSO owns the grants it creates and deactivates the ones that stop matching, never touching admin-created grants; a mapping row may target a project, project site or org unit, pinned or resolved from a second claim; a claim mapping can never grant the global admin role; SSO is additive federation with no mandatory enforcement; jmespath and pyjwt are permitted dependencies (Authlib rejected), and the previously recorded 'standard library only' constraint applied to a different area and is cleared.

Verified repo facts: va_users has no external-identity column; authorization is va_user_access_grants rows (role + scope_type in global|project|project_site|org_unit, active/deactive, no expiry); mas_org_unit is project-scoped with an LTREE path so one org-unit grant covers a subtree; mas_odk_connections is the per-external-system config precedent with Fernet-encrypted secrets; requests, cryptography, flask-caching and Flask-Limiter are already declared; the migration head is c7a4e2d9f1b6.

Full plan with data model, login flow, claim extraction, provider matrix, phases, test plan, verification gates, deferred items and rejected alternatives: .tasks/2026-09-26-project-sso-oauth2.md. No application code written yet; the policy baseline docs/policy/project-sso-oauth2.md is phase 0 and must be written before implementation.

title: Re-derive submission validity on the server instead of trusting the client boolean
description:
web_intake_service.py:796-797 is the whole server-side validity gate: if completion.get('valid') is not True: raise. The browser computes that boolean; the server never re-derives it. With the Python evaluator from digitva-cal.1 in place, the server can evaluate relevant and constraint itself over the submitted answers and stop trusting the client.

Threat model, stated: interviewers are authenticated staff, not the public, so this is not an open-internet hole. It is still a gate that does nothing, and a crafted request can store a date of death before the date of birth or an ABHA number failing its regex.
design:
DECIDED by the owner 2026-09-20, two parts.

PART 1 -- log and accept, do not reject. The first release evaluates relevant and constraint server-side but does NOT refuse a submission that only the server considers invalid. It records the disagreement and stores the answers. Reason: if the server starts rejecting what the client accepted, an interviewer in the field is stuck with no recourse and no way to complete a death record. Once the real mismatch volume is known from live data, a later release can flip to refusing -- that flip is a separate decision, not part of this bead.

The client's own boolean keeps its existing power in one direction only: if the client says invalid, the submission is still refused, exactly as today. The server never accepts that boolean as PROOF of validity.

PART 2 -- record each mismatch as a validation_err on the response itself, not only in a log line. A log is not queryable, rotates away, and nobody reads it; the point is to learn how often the two engines disagree and on which questions, which means the data has to live with the submission. Additive, reversible migration.

Each entry carries: the question name, which rule disagreed (relevant or constraint), and that the client claimed valid. It carries NO answer values -- these records are PII and a validation error must not become a side channel that copies answers into a new column, an export or a log. Also return the entries in the HTTP response to the submitting client, which costs nothing and makes a field problem debuggable.

Open sub-question for whoever implements: whether validation_err belongs on va_submissions or on va_submission_payload_versions. Prefer the payload version if a resubmission should be able to disagree differently from its predecessor -- that is the more useful history. State the choice and why.
acceptance_criteria: A submission whose answers violate a constraint is STORED, not refused, when the payload claims valid=true, and carries a validation_err entry naming the question and the rule. A submission the client marks invalid is still refused. Valid submissions carry no entries and are unaffected -- prove that against the existing web-intake tests. No answer values in the stored entries, the HTTP response, or any log line. Migration is additive and reversible.
notes:
Blocked on digitva-cal.1 (the Python evaluator). Sequencing note: a later release may flip from accept-and-record to refuse; the data this bead collects is what should inform that, so do not build the refusal path now. Settled 2026-09-20: validation_err lives on va_submission_payload_versions, not va_submissions. That table is genuinely per-version, with a version_status lifecycle (active / pending_upstream / superseded / rejected) and a unique-active index per va_sid, so a resubmission creates a new version and its disagreement record belongs with the answers it describes rather than being overwritten on the parent row. Storing it on va_submissions would lose the history that makes the accept-and-record release worth doing.

When adding the column, do not repeat the doubled-constraint-name bug catalogued in the CHECK-constraint bead: pass only the discriminator to any new constraint, never the ck_<table>_ prefixed form.

---
Implemented 2026-09-20: app/services/web_form_relevance_service.py (new), wired into web_intake_service.submit_draft. Migration f2031819b3aa adds va_submission_payload_versions.validation_err (JSONB, additive/reversible, round-tripped clean). Route returns validation_err in submit response. Tests: tests/services/test_web_form_relevance_service.py, additions to test_web_intake_service.py and test_intake_api.py. Full suite: 1696 passed, PYTEST_EXIT=0. Not closed per instructions.

title: Port the XLSForm expression evaluator to Python, with a conformance corpus
description:
Decided by the owner 2026-09-20: Python must parse the instrument JSON and assess response validity itself, so the browser stops being the single enforcement point (digitva-cal). This is step one -- the evaluator alone, no behaviour change to intake yet.

Scope is bounded and known. vendor/who-va-2022/src/engine/expression.ts is 402 lines. The instrument carries 445 expressions, 277 unique, across three fields: relevant (318), constraint (89), calculation (38). The complete function set used is: selected, if, not, and, or, regex, today, date, int, string-length, count-selected. Nothing else appears.
design:
THE CENTRAL RISK is two evaluators that drift, which is exactly what the expression-tokenizer bug in 78757d4 showed can happen invisibly. The port is only acceptable if divergence fails a test.

So the deliverable is two things, and the corpus matters more than the port:
1. A conformance corpus GENERATED FROM THE TYPESCRIPT ENGINE: every unique expression in the instrument, evaluated against a set of answer fixtures, with its result recorded as golden output in a committed JSON file. A tooling script under tooling/who-va-2022/ produces it, deterministically, the way build-layer-reference.mjs does.
2. A Python evaluator asserted against that corpus, case by case. A test that reads the corpus and requires identical results for every case, including error cases.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE TRAPS, found by inspection 2026-09-20 -- each needs a corpus case:
* Python re matches Unicode digits with \\d by default; JavaScript RegExp does not. The instrument contains regex(.,'^(?!0{1,3}$)\\d{1,3}$') on sa13-sa19, so a Devanagari or Bengali digit would pass server-side and fail client-side. Use re.ASCII or explicit ASCII classes and pin it with a case.
* XPath 1.0 string literals have no escape mechanism; a backslash is an ordinary character (established in 78757d4). The doubled-quote convention is the only escape.
* today() and date arithmetic: timezone handling must match, and the app is timezone-aware throughout.
* Empty and missing answers: isEmpty/asBoolean/asNumber/equal in expression.ts have specific coercion semantics. Port them literally rather than reaching for Python truthiness.
* Numeric comparison of ISO date strings via dateNumber.

No change to web_intake_service or session behaviour in this work package. Evaluator plus corpus plus tests only.
acceptance_criteria: A committed corpus covering all 277 unique instrument expressions with golden results from the TypeScript engine. A Python evaluator that reproduces every one. Regenerating the corpus on an unmodified tree reproduces it byte for byte. Reverting any single semantic fix in the Python evaluator fails at least one corpus case -- demonstrate that, do not assert it.
close_reason: Landed in e77c293. Python evaluator plus a conformance corpus of 347 unique expressions and 1,903 cases generated from the TypeScript engine, pinned byte for byte and asserted case by case. Distribution confirms it is not vacuous (334 true, 1,351 false, 60 NaN, 59 strings). The deliberate-regression requirement was met by demonstration, reproduced independently in the main session: removing the six re.ASCII guards reports '1 of 1903 corpus cases diverged'; restoring them passes. Surfaced a second Unicode-digit bug in the tokenizer's own numeric-literal detection. Two unportable JS behaviours recorded rather than hidden. digitva-cal.2 (server-side validity, accept-and-record) is now unblocked.

title: Machine-translated strings must not be served until a human reviews them
description:
Migration b6d2f4a9c1e7 seeded 214 machine-translated strings with source='imported' -- the same value workbook-sourced strings carry. Nothing in the database distinguishes 'came from a deployed ODK form' from 'Claude wrote it', and approval is per-locale, so approving a locale blesses both at once. On the owner's dev database all thirteen locales are approved and active, which means unreviewed machine translations are being served to web forms right now.

Owner's intent, stated 2026-09-20: only the workbook-imported translations are approved; the machine-translated ones need review. They must remain visible and editable in the panel -- deletion is explicitly not wanted, because it removes the very content someone has to review.
design:
Third source value SOURCE_MACHINE = 'machine' (source is String(16), no CHECK constraint, so no widening needed).

1. Migration relabels the 214 seeded rows imported -> machine, matching on the exact literals from b6d2f4a9c1e7 so a row an administrator has already corrected or that no longer matches is left alone. Reversible.
2. export_translations excludes source='machine', so the served payload omits them and the client falls back to English per string -- the same mechanism an untranslated string already uses. This is the whole fix: the strings exist, are listed, are editable, and are not served.
3. The panel marks machine rows distinctly and offers an accept-as-is action that promotes machine -> edited without retyping. update_string already sets edited, so an admin who edits the text is already covered; the gap is only accepting a good machine string unchanged.
4. A workbook re-import must overwrite a machine row: workbook beats machine, while edited still beats both. Today the importer keeps edited and overwrites imported; machine must join the overwritable side.
5. Per-extension coverage should not count machine rows as translated, or the panel will report a locale as complete on strings that are not being served.
acceptance_criteria: A locale with machine rows serves English for exactly those items and its own workbook translations for the rest. The panel lists machine rows, marks them, and can promote one to edited. A workbook re-import overwrites a machine row and never an edited one. Coverage does not count machine rows. Tests pin each of these.
close_reason: Machine-translated strings are now a distinct source='machine', relabelled by migration c1a4b6e8d3f2, excluded from export_translations and from coverage, visible and acceptable in the panel via POST .../strings/accept. Precedence edited > imported > machine holds without importer changes (only SOURCE_EDITED was ever special-cased). Constraint renamed to ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved by d2b5c7f9e4a3 and the model now passes only the discriminator. Review found one real gap, fixed before commit: export_xliff labelled machine rows state='translated', so a CAT tool showed unreviewed drafts as finished; they now export as initial with subState digitva:machine, and an unmapped source understates rather than claiming translated.

title: Web form locale codes: column default 'en' is not a seeded mas_languages code
description: va_project_master.web_intake_default_locale defaults to 'en' (model and migration f2a9c4d7e1b3) but flask seed run creates mas_languages codes 'english', 'hindi', ... (app/commands/seed.py). Consequences on every seeded deployment: (1) the form-options resolver in app/routes/api/organization.py logs 'en is not an active language' and falls back to the first active code, so on dev every project's web form opens with locale='assamese'; (2) the projects admin panel now shows 'en (inactive)' and blocks Save until an admin picks an active code. Decide: either seed short locale codes / add a locale_code column on mas_languages that the resolver serves, or map at the endpoint. Domain decision, not for an agent to take.
design: Decided 2026-09-19 with the owner: 'en' is the system default web-form language on every project and is always available; a project ADDS languages from the set the bundled instrument actually has translations for (an explicit registry in Python, asserted against the bundle by a test), not from mas_languages; the interviewer picks a working language on the intake page, remembered in the browser (localStorage, last choice wins), falling back to 'en' when the remembered code is not in the project's list. Narration languages stay on mas_languages: they describe the recording, not the screen. No migration.

title: Help pages don't explain how ICD codes reach VA causes at report time
description: Checked 2026-10-23 against code. (1) app/templates/help/pages/cod-buckets.html never mentions ICD-11 (0 matches); it describes buckets as mapping 'one or more ICD-10 codes', although WHO_2022_VA_2026 maps 18,505 ICD-11 codes and DORIS projects code in ICD-11. (2) No help page says that an ICD-11 code without its own map row reports under its nearest mapped ICD-11 parent (the ancestor walk in the COD snapshot view and the report path). On staging, 445 of 655 distinct coded codes resolve this way. (3) No page states that reporting never crosswalks ICD-11 <-> ICD-10: each case is bucketed from the classification it was coded in, and SmartVA's ICD-10 causes through the ICD-10 rows. The WHO 11To10 table is used only to draft ICD-11 rows for expert review (flask cod-buckets generator) and as a 'follows its ICD-10 equivalent' review reason in the origin legend. Fix: update cod-buckets.html and va-code-mappings.html / _origin_legend.html to describe the actual resolution order (direct row, then nearest mapped ICD-11 parent, else unmatched) and the drafting-only role of the crosswalk. Cross-check against the ancestor-chain MV work and digitva-mubf (rule mismatch between the snapshot view and reports). Docs-only change; keep docs/policy/icd10-to-icd11-transition.md consistent.

title: COD reports and COD snapshot view resolve ICD-11 buckets against different map rows
description: Found 2026-10-23 by the COD snapshot MV refresh session. title: Messages inbox API the app polls (no third-party push)
description: Owner 2026-10-04: no Google FCM or Expo push; a Flask messages API the app polls. GET /api/v1/me/messages?after=<cursor> -> {messages:[{id, kind, created_at, project_id, death_id?, draft_id?}], next_cursor}; per-user rows written by events that already happen (revision_requested, superseded, other_draft_started on a case I hold, form_version_available, case_registered_in_my_unit, case_reopened); ids and kinds only, no names/phones/answers. App polls on foreground, about every 60 s while open, and from an Android WorkManager background task (expo-background-task, no Google push), then runs its normal /api/v1 sync; the inbox is a nudge, sync stays the source of truth, a missed poll costs nothing. Empty poll must be one indexed query (user_id, id). Retention: purge after 30 days. Session revoke needs no message (any call answers 401 session_revoked). Gunicorn runs -w 1 sync, so no long-poll/SSE: short polls only. Migration for the table. Self-hosted ntfy/UnifiedPush parked unless field delay proves too long.
notes:
Owner 2026-10-04: use Redis. Redesign: no table, no migration. One Redis stream per user (digitva_msg:<user_id>, XADD MAXLEN ~100, EXPIRE 30 days); poll = XRANGE after the cursor, zero DB queries. Redis here is 64 MB allkeys-lru, so messages can be evicted: a cursor older than the stream's first id answers reset: true and the app runs a full sync. Every user-visible state (sent back, superseded, other draft) must also be in the synced data; the stream is only a nudge.
Owner 2026-10-04 (supersedes the Redis-stream note): notifications live in Postgres; Redis only speeds up serving. Table (migration): bigint identity id, user_id, kind, project_id, death_id null, draft_id null, created_at; index (user_id, id); ids and kinds only, no PII. Row inserted in the same transaction as the event that causes it. Redis keeps per-user latest id (digitva_msg:last:<user_id>), set after commit, short TTL (~5 min) so a failed or stale set heals itself; poll with cursor >= cached latest answers empty with no DB query; cache miss or newer id -> one indexed DB read. Purge rows older than 30 days in a daily batched Celery delete. Cursor = last id; no reset needed since the DB is the truth.
Server committed. Open until app half digitva-hdrv.1 lands. Beat row seeds on next celery worker restart.

title: Android: PIN lockout instead of wipe; PIN reset after password sign-in keeps the interviews
description: Owner 2026-10-01 (Path B, docs/policy/field-data-collection.md). Replace 'five wrong PINs wipe that store' with a timed lock (suggested 15 min, escalating). Wipe stays only on session_revoked. A user who forgets the PIN can reset it after re-authenticating (password + second factor) and keeps their unsynced interviews. Design consequence: the store key can no longer be derived from the PIN; use a random data key wrapped by the Keystore secret and the PIN, re-wrapped on reset. Policy baseline in field-data-collection.md first (also lines about key derivation, 5-wrong wipe), then mobile/digitva-collect, with jest tests.
notes:
Owner 2026-10-01: option 2. Interviews on a handset are shared by interviewers in the same scope (including unsynced ones); not private per interviewer. This reverses the per-interviewer encryption in field-data-collection.md (lines ~69-75, 131-133, 159-161). Suggested design: one data key per scope (project/site/unit) on the device, wrapped separately by each interviewer's PIN, so any interviewer in that scope can unlock it, PIN reset re-wraps only that user's copy, and an interviewer outside the scope cannot open it at all (cryptographic, not just a UI filter). Needs the policy rewritten first; DM/supervisor audit trail must still record which interviewer did each interview.
Owner 2026-10-01: simplest design. Server supplies one data key per scope (e.g. district) at sign-in; the app keeps it in the Android Keystore (user-auth gated) and encrypts the shared device store with it. PIN is only the unlock gate, not part of the key, so PIN reset needs no re-wrapping. Key cached for offline use; rotation per scope, phones re-encrypt at next sync; wipe only on session_revoked. Supersedes the per-user wrapped-key suggestion above. Server needs a key endpoint (never log keys; store encrypted at rest).
Owner 2026-10-01: PIN is exactly 6 digits (was 6-16). Update field-data-collection.md and mobile/digitva-collect validation, tests.
Owner 2026-10-01: enrolment codes are not admin-only. A data_manager at any unit level can create them, for staff under their own unit (e.g. a PHC MO enrols the staff below). Code must be limited to the creator's unit subtree; reuse the unit-scoped data_manager access from digitva-djd; audit who created each code. Replaces 'admin-only enrolment codes' in field-data-collection.md. Note the existing caveat that data managers cannot give unit grants stays separate: a code enrols a device, it grants no role.
Owner 2026-10-01: accepted C4. Self-signed release key, held and backed up by the owner. With this, all Path B points are decided; mark docs/policy/field-data-collection.md Path B accepted once it is rewritten for: 6-digit PIN, timed lock (no wrong-PIN wipe), server-issued per-scope data key, shared store per scope, data_manager-issued enrolment codes.

title: Password reset links can be reused within their hour
description: app/services/token_service.py issues stateless itsdangerous tokens; app/routes/va_auth.py reset_password (~line 115) sets the password but nothing invalidates the token, so a leaked or forwarded reset link can set the password again until it expires (1 h). Fix without a new table: sign a fingerprint of the current password hash (and later the factor state) into password_reset tokens and reject the token when it no longer matches, so it dies on first use. title: Rebuild the translation editor as a per-question workspace
description:
Owner's design, 2026-09-21. The current editor is a flat, alphabetical list of strings with an inline textarea per row. Replace it with a list ordered the way the questionnaire is ordered, where each row is a QUESTION and editing opens a modal carrying that question's whole package: label, hint, constraint message, and the options of any choice list it uses. Reviewing a translation then means reviewing a complete unit rather than a string torn out of context -- which is exactly how the Odia and Hindi defects escaped notice.

LIST VIEW: read-only. Columns, in this order: question code, English label, the locale's label. Ordered by the question's position in the form, not alphabetically. Paginate 50 questions per page (note: pagination unit changes from strings to questions).

MODAL: opens for one question and holds every translatable item for it -- label, hint, constraint message, and each option of its choice list. Save writes them together.

CHOICE LISTS ARE SHARED: a list belongs to many questions (YES_NO_DK_REF backs 224). Editing an option updates it for every question that uses that list -- which is already how storage works, keyed by list_name/value. The modal must SAY so, with the count, or an editor will believe they are making a local change.

RICH TEXT: the source carries ODK markup -- 337 questions have <span style="color:blue"> in guidance, 51 hints and 6 labels carry HTML. The list and modal must RENDER it, not display raw tags, and the modal needs a toolbar for bold, italic and coloured span.
design:
THREE DEPENDENCIES, none of them optional.

1. CONSTRAINT MESSAGES DO NOT EXIST AS TRANSLATIONS. 89 of 449 questions carry one; the field is not in _TRANSLATABLE_FIELDS, zero rows are stored, and NO deployed workbook has a constraint_message:: column in any language -- so there is nothing to import. Putting them in the modal means adding the field to the translatable set AND authoring the target text, the way the DigitVA layer strings were authored. Until then the modal can show the English read-only, but the owner should decide which.

2. ORDERING AND GROUPING NEED THE INSTRUMENT. map_instrument_translations stores item_kind/item_key/field with no notion of question order or which list a question uses. list_strings returns flat rows. The panel must join against the generated instrument JSON (which has order, listName and choices) to sort by form position and to group options under their questions. That is the real work in this issue.

3. THE RENDERER ALREADY EXISTS -- REUSE IT. vendor/who-va-2022/src/ui/rich-text.ts parses exactly this markup into styled spans and deliberately avoids innerHTML so hostile content degrades to visible text. It is NOT currently exported from the built bundle. Re-export parseRichText from tooling/who-va-2022/entry.mjs rather than writing a second parser for the admin page: two renderers would drift, and the admin editor showing something different from the form is the failure this whole issue exists to prevent. The toolbar must emit the same subset that parser accepts, or an editor will produce markup the form renders as literal text.

Guidance is a fourth, smaller gap: the service lists it as translatable and 338 questions have it, but zero rows exist because the workbooks ship guidance_hint::English only.
acceptance_criteria: List ordered by form position, 50 questions per page, columns question code / English / locale text, read-only, markup rendered. Modal edits a question's label, hint and choice options together and states how many questions share each list. Rich-text toolbar emits only what parseRichText accepts. Constraint messages either editable or explicitly shown read-only per the owner's decision.
notes:
CLARIFIED 2026-09-21 (owner): the Google Translate button is PER TEXT, not per question. Each individual text in the modal -- the question label, the hint, each choice option, the read-only guidance and constraint message -- carries its own small button beside it, and clicking it opens Google Translate with THAT ONE FIELD's English only. Nothing is concatenated: no 'translate the whole question', no bundling label with hint. The editor is working on one field at a time and wants that field's text.

This also mostly dissolves the URL-length worry recorded earlier: a single label or choice option is short. Only a long guidance block can approach a problematic URL, and guidance is read-only anyway, so if any field needs truncation or omission it is that one.
close_reason: Delivered in 5618e07. Own page at /admin/instrument-translations/<instrument>/<locale> with page and search in the URL; one row per question in form order (code, English, locale text) covering all 449 WHO questions plus 80 DigitVA layer questions and 10 orphan choice lists, 536 rows for hi; modal edits label, hint and choice options, shows constraint message and guidance read-only badged untranslated, warns how many questions a shared list changes, and offers Save, Save and next, Undo and Close with dirty tracking; per-field Google Translate links, hidden for Khasi; markup rendered through the form's own parseRichText, re-exported from the bundle rather than reimplemented. Full suite 1729 passed; verified in a browser rather than on report. The authoring of untranslated constraint messages and guidance was detached to its own issue: it is independent work, not unfinished work here.

title: Dev database's va_user_access_grants CHECK omits collaborator_pii
description:
Found 2026-09-20 while verifying that renaming CHECK constraints preserved their logic -- the rename did not cause this, it merely exposed it.

Comparing pg_get_constraintdef between the dev database and a database built from the migration chain alone:

  dev:   role = ANY (ARRAY['collaborator', 'coder', 'coding_tester', 'reviewer', 'data_manager', 'interviewer'])
  fresh: role = ANY (ARRAY['collaborator', 'collaborator_pii', 'coder', 'coding_tester', 'reviewer', 'data_manager', 'interviewer'])

So on dev, inserting a va_user_access_grants row with role='collaborator_pii' is refused by the database, while a fresh deployment accepts it. The scope_shape and role_scope constraints are the ones guarding authorization shape, so this is an authorization-relevant divergence, not cosmetic.

The test suite cannot see it: tests build their schema with db.create_all() from the models, never from the migration chain, and tests/migrations/test_schema_drift.py compares a fresh migration-built database against the models -- neither ever inspects the long-lived dev database. So dev can drift from both without any test noticing.
design:
First establish which is correct: does the model declare collaborator_pii, and did a migration add it that dev never received, or was it removed from dev by hand? git log -S collaborator_pii over the migrations and the model will say.

If a migration adds it and dev simply missed it, the fix is operational -- replay the migration on dev -- not a code change. If no migration adds it, then a fresh install and the models are ahead of every migration, which is a real chain gap and needs one.

Related but distinct from digitva-2g7 (dev and a fresh clone differing on the old WHO_2022_VA bucket scheme). The two together suggest the dev database has accumulated more than one divergence from its own migration history, which is worth a single sweep comparing dev against a fresh replay across all constraints, defaults and enums rather than finding them one at a time.
acceptance_criteria: The correct definition is established from the migration history, dev matches it, and it is recorded whether this was operational drift or a missing migration. If a sweep is done, its findings are filed.
notes:
TRACED 2026-09-20: this is operational drift on the dev database, not a missing migration. Two committed migrations carry the role -- f1c6a9d3e7b5_add_collaborator_pii_role.py (added in c04662c) and a40c38e73af4_add_org_unit_coding_gate.py (3a17d8c) -- and the dev database is long past both, since f1c6a9d3e7b5 is the root of the chain recorded in handoff.md. A database built from the chain alone has the role; dev does not. So dev's constraint was recreated or altered outside the chain at some point.

Fix is therefore operational for dev: bring that one constraint into line with what the migrations produce. No application change. Worth doing the wider dev-versus-fresh sweep described in the design field at the same time, because two independent divergences (this and digitva-2g7) is evidence of a pattern rather than an accident.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-09-20 (not closing per instructions -- leaving for owner to close):

Part 1: migration 120f783ea138 (chains onto f2031819b3aa, single head) repairs
both the CHECK constraint and the access_role_enum label idempotently -- reads
pg_get_constraintdef first, only acts when collaborator_pii is absent from it,
and uses ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS for the enum. Verified on a scratch database
(minerva_migration_verify, dropped after): built from the chain to f2031819b3aa,

with a clean (undoubled) constraint name; re-invoked the migration's upgrade()
directly against the now-correct state -> same constraint oid, unchanged (true
no-op). A collaborator_pii/project insert succeeds against the repaired
constraint; collaborator_pii/global (invalid scope) is rejected. Applied to the
actual dev `minerva` database -- constraint and enum are now correct there.

Part 2: `flask schema drift-check` (app/commands/schema_drift.py) builds the
same throwaway migration-chain database test_schema_drift.py does and diffs it
against whatever database it's pointed at, on CHECK constraint names+text,
column defaults, and enum members -- normalizing Postgres's equivalent-but-
differently-spelled cast/paren forms first (see docstring) so it doesn't cry
wolf. Read-only on target; own scratch db only.

Run against dev before the migration was applied: found exactly this
constraint (missing collaborator_pii) and the enum missing the same label --
